blocks.content: • Species Richness – total number of species in a region.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Species Richness measures the total number of species present in a specific region.
Species Evenness evaluates how individual organisms are distributed among species.
Alpha, Beta, and Gamma diversity measure ecological diversity at local, comparative, and regional scales.
Endemism refers to species that are exclusive to a defined geographic area.

blocks.content: Endemism – species restricted to a specific geographic area.
• Species Evenness – distribution of individuals among species.

rows: Overall diversity within a large geographic region.

blocks.content: • Alpha Diversity – diversity within a particular habitat.
• Beta Diversity – comparison of diversity between ecosystems.

items: Alpha Diversity is measured within a specific habitat, whereas Beta Diversity compares changes between ecosystems.
Gamma Diversity encompasses the total overall diversity across a broad geographic area.
Questions often distinguish between Species Richness (count of species) and Species Evenness (relative abundance of each species).

blocks.content: • Gamma Diversity – overall diversity within a large geographic region.
• Endemism – species restricted to a specific geographic area.
